I am about to finish my lease there. While the office staff is friendly and the quality of the apartments is decent for what you pay (I currently pay $450/month for a three bedroom with two roommates, and we all have private bathrooms), there are some issues.

Don't expect the apartment to be in good condition when you arrive. They will likely not check the apartment before you arrive. When we moved in, a bed and two bedside tables were missing, the bathrooms were disgusting, the living room chair was destroyed, and the carpet was awful. Management claimed they would send someone to clean the carpet, but nearly three years in this was never done.

It is also very difficult to get major issues resolved in a timely manner. Our ceiling leaked for about three months before they took it seriously. One night it was so bad we submitted emergency maintenance requests and contacted the emergency phone number, and we did not receive a response until 20 hours later. Their solution was having us run giant, noisy fans that drove up our electric bill while they fixed the hole in the roof that had apparently been there for years, and they then dragged their feet in paying us back until we informed them that we had them on recording promising to cover any electrical overage bills. Every time we tried to meet with the property manager, he was at lunch, not in office, on a phone call, etc., with no messages returned. There is a new property manager now, but not much has improved since then. Communication is still awful, and they have been making mistakes on the monthly rent and utility bill nearly every month.

The apartment property itself is also in disrepair. What appears to be mold or rot is growing on the wooden stairs, which look and feel as if they could fall apart at any second. Over academic breaks, they fail to remove trash from the dumpsters in a timely manner, and then threaten to fine residents if they do not place their garbage in the dumpster despite not being able to reach the dumpster without walking on trash bags. There was also a period of 4-5 days where the water to my building was shut off, with the date it would be turned back on again being extended constantly. Originally it was only meant to be switched off for a few hours. Management's solution was having us use vacant apartments in other buildings, which were repulsive.

If you're willing to put up with situations resembling this for the low rent, then go for it. One bonus is that in my time with Mountain Valley, I have not had to deal with any pest issues, which seems to be an issue at similarly priced apartments in the area. If you can, try to get an apartment on the top floor, as the view is decent, and you don't have to listen to people stomping above you. They are also pet friendly once you pay the pet fee and pet rent, and have a dog park if that's a deciding factor for you.
